name: THE BLAME PIE
title: THE BLAME PIE
challenge: Self-blame, guilt & shame
moment: Self-blame, guilt & shame
mechanism: Imagine A Pie → Check The Whole → Choose Repair
goal: Own your real share of a problem without carrying everyone else's; sequence shared priorities.
steps:
1. Imagine a pie that stands for everything that caused the situation.
2. In your mind, give slices to your choices, other people, circumstances, systems, timing, and chance.
3. Make sure all slices together equal 100.
4. Focus only on your true share.
5. Picture one repair for your slice. Let the rest stay outside your responsibility.

name: THE LIFE DIRECTION TEST
title: THE LIFE DIRECTION TEST
challenge: Values, meaning & loss
moment: Values, meaning & loss
mechanism: Picture → Name Likely → Select Direction
goal: Choose the next hour by direction, not by the loudest thought — calibrate shared timing.

name: CLOSE ONE DOOR FOR THIRTY SECONDS
title: CLOSE ONE DOOR FOR THIRTY SECONDS
challenge: Urgency & decision pressure
moment: Urgency & decision pressure
mechanism: Close Door → Reopen Choice → Choose Next
goal: Resync right timing: test each leading option briefly to learn from your reaction without committing.
steps:
1. Picture the two leading options. Mentally fade one for thirty seconds and pretend it is unavailable; do not commit.
2. Notice the first specific reaction—relief, disappointment, bargaining, urgency, or no change. Name it in four words or fewer.
3. Bring that option back. Repeat once with the other option faded so both reactions receive the same test.
4. Use the clearer reaction as one piece of data, then choose only the next responsible move.

name: THE CONTROL GRAVEYARD
title: THE CONTROL GRAVEYARD
challenge: Uncertainty & reassurance seeking
moment: Uncertainty & reassurance seeking
mechanism: Use Control → Focus On Costs → Choose Experiment
goal: Notice which control habits charge more over time than they repay now; order next steps.
steps:
1. Name everything used to control the feeling: checking, avoiding, numbing, arguing, extra certainty, overworking.
2. Beside each, picture the short-term payoff and the six-month bill.
3. Focus on any method whose bill exceeds its relief.
4. Choose one experiment in not paying that cost today.

name: MORE THAN THIS STATE
title: MORE THAN THIS STATE
challenge: A failure feels like proof of who you are
moment: A failure feels like proof of who you are
mechanism: Carry Qualities → Place Painful → Ask Part
goal: Put the current painful state back inside a larger picture of you — calibrate shared sequence.
steps:

name: ONE NOTCH, NOT THE STORY
title: ONE NOTCH, NOT THE STORY
challenge: Trauma & memory-as-present
moment: Trauma & memory-as-present
mechanism: Rate Alarm → Use External Cue → Re-rate Once → Stop
goal: Lower the current alarm one notch without touching the memory itself — coordinate clean timing.
steps:
1. Rate the current alarm from 0 to 10 without explaining why.
2. Pick one present-day cue: your feet, cool water, a stable surface, or a familiar voice.
3. Use that cue for twenty seconds while keeping your eyes open.
4. Rate the alarm once more and stop; no memory review is required.

name: MATCH THE PRESSURE, THEN ZERO IT
title: MATCH THE PRESSURE, THEN ZERO IT
challenge: Body-state misreading
moment: Body-state misreading
mechanism: Press Equal → Step Down → Reach Zero
goal: Balance real choices: match two sides of physical pressure, then lower both together back to zero.
steps:
1. Press palms together—or both hands into one cushion—at about twenty percent effort. Keep breathing ordinary.
2. Adjust until neither side wins and the pressure feels equal. Hold that match for two seconds.
3. Lower both sides together through three gentle levels: fifteen, ten, then five percent.
4. Reach zero, rest both hands on a stable surface, and observe whether the urge to press returns.

name: THE BORING DOSE
title: THE BORING DOSE
challenge: Getting pulled away every few minutes
moment: Getting pulled away every few minutes
mechanism: Choose Safe → Stay Boredom → Raise the Dose
goal: Practise a small, fixed dose of boredom without adding stimulation or extending the challenge — sequence mixed signals.

name: THE TURNING POINT AT HALF SPEED
title: THE TURNING POINT AT HALF SPEED
challenge: Evidence distortion & selective thinking
moment: Evidence distortion & selective thinking
mechanism: Recall Exchange → Shift → Keep Fact
goal: Review only the turning point slowly enough to keep observation separate from motive; order right sequence.
steps:
1. Choose no more than ten seconds of the interaction, beginning before the moment that felt different.
2. Run those ten seconds once in imagination at half speed. Keep only what you can actually observe: words, pauses, volume, face, and movement.
3. End at the first change and name it without motive: ‘the pause lengthened,’ ‘the volume rose,’ or ‘the reply shortened.’
4. Keep that one fact. End the review before building another explanation.

challenge: Urgency & decision pressure
moment: Urgency & decision pressure
mechanism: Let Active → Protect Block → Update Evidence
goal: Make active concerns compete for one attention block using consequence and reversibility, not noise — coordinate mixed inputs.
steps:
1. Let each active concern bid on urgency, consequence, reversibility, and information value.
2. Total the four ratings.
3. Award one protected block to the highest bidder and deny all others entry until time expires.
4. Re-auction with updated evidence.

name: TURN THE LOOP INTO FIVE ICONS
title: TURN THE LOOP INTO FIVE ICONS
challenge: Rumination & worry loops
moment: Rumination & worry loops
mechanism: No Sentences → Spot The Return → Choose An Exit
goal: Tune shared inputs; turn a repetitive thought loop into simple images and interrupt the first repeated meaning.
steps:
1. Imagine five boxes. Do not use full sentences.
2. Give each of the last five thought turns one simple inner picture.
3. Notice the first picture whose meaning comes back later.
4. At the next box, picture one real fact to check or one small action to take, then stop imagining.

name: SCULPT THE PROBLEM
title: SCULPT THE PROBLEM
challenge: Action avoidance & procrastination
moment: Action avoidance & procrastination
mechanism: Use Small → Move Object → Name Real
goal: Move one imagined part of a problem and translate that spatial shift into a real action — order usable sequence.
steps:
1. Picture the problem as positions for people, obstacles, resources, and goals.
2. Place those positions as they feel now.
3. Move only one position or distance toward a more workable configuration.
4. Name the real-life action that matches that imagined shift.

name: REMEMBER THE FUTURE IN ADVANCE
title: REMEMBER THE FUTURE IN ADVANCE
challenge: Staring at a task but not beginning
moment: Staring at a task but not beginning
mechanism: Sensory disconnection family: create memory opens a route toward look backward.
goal: Imagine the scene just after completion, then trace backward to the first movement you can do now; resync clean timing.
steps:
1. Create a memory-like scene set just after completing the action.
2. Include time, location, body posture, one sensory cue, along with what you did when difficulty appeared.
3. Look backward from that imagined completion to the first real movement and do it now.

name: INTERVIEW THE OBSTACLE
title: INTERVIEW THE OBSTACLE
challenge: Action avoidance & procrastination
moment: Action avoidance & procrastination
mechanism: Give Obstacle → Make Step → Picture Negotiate
goal: Calibrate shared choices: ask the obstacle what it is protecting and negotiate one step that respects the valid need.
steps:
1. Give the obstacle a character and ask three questions: What are you protecting.
2. What do you fear will happen.
3. What would make one step acceptable.
4. Picture its answers, then negotiate a small step that protects the valid need without handing over total control.

moment: Urges, impulses & cravings

name: BORROW ONE MOVE FROM THE AVATAR
title: BORROW ONE MOVE FROM THE AVATAR
challenge: You are trying to become what others expect
moment: You are trying to become what others expect
mechanism: Posture–mood locking family: create figure opens a route toward borrow one move.
goal: Borrow one useful behaviour from an imagined capable figure without trying to become them — tune mixed signals.
steps:
1. Create a figure who represents the needed capacity—steady, playful, discerning, brave.
2. Give it posture, voice, and one signature behaviour.
3. Borrow only that behaviour for this situation. Becoming the character is unnecessary.

name: BUILD THE MINIATURE FIRST
title: BUILD THE MINIATURE FIRST
challenge: You are afraid of choosing wrong
moment: You are afraid of choosing wrong
mechanism: Automatic-pattern blindness family: create low opens a route toward test miniature.
goal: Resync usable sequence; test a low-risk miniature of the idea before paying the full cost of the real version.
steps:
1. Create a low-risk scaled version: a one-day routine, sample client, temporary location, trial budget, or mock conversation.
2. State what the prototype must reveal and the maximum cost.
3. Test the miniature, collect feedback, and redesign before expanding it.

name: PUT TIME ARROWS ON THE OPTIONS
title: PUT TIME ARROWS ON THE OPTIONS
challenge: You are stuck between two reasonable options
moment: You are stuck between two reasonable options
mechanism: Automatic-pattern blindness family: option opens a route toward follow time arrows.
goal: Notice which options improve, decay, stay stable, or expire as time passes — order working inputs.
steps:
1. Notice every option as improving, stable, decaying, or expiring with delay.
2. Add the date or condition where its arrow changes.
3. Sequence decisions around genuine expiry rather than anxiety’s false deadlines.

name: WHAT WOULD THIS FACT CHANGE?
title: WHAT WOULD THIS FACT CHANGE?
challenge: Action avoidance & procrastination
moment: Action avoidance & procrastination
mechanism: Action avoidance family: point positive opens a route toward test relevance.
goal: Order shared sequence; collect only facts that could actually change what you decide.
steps:
1. For every desired data point, picture how a positive, negative, or neutral result would alter the decision.
2. If no result changes action, stop collecting it.
3. Prioritise the fact with the largest possible decision swing.

name: RUN A TWO-OPTION KNOCKOUT
title: RUN A TWO-OPTION KNOCKOUT
challenge: Too many tasks are competing at once
moment: Too many tasks are competing at once
mechanism: Seed Options → Play Pairs → Crown Next
goal: Compare two options at a time using one declared criterion and let the survivor earn the next look; resync signals.
steps:
1. Picture the available options into a simple bracket. Give an unpaired option a bye rather than inventing a rival.
2. Choose one criterion that matters for this round and picture it above the bracket. Do not switch it mid-game.
3. Compare only two options at a time. Advance the one that better meets the declared criterion.
4. Crown the final survivor as the next option to inspect or act on—not as a permanent life verdict.

name: THE PAST INVESTMENT GETS NO NEW VOTE
title: THE PAST INVESTMENT GETS NO NEW VOTE
challenge: Evidence distortion & selective thinking
moment: Evidence distortion & selective thinking
mechanism: Sunk-cost thinking family: hide already opens a route toward remove sunk vote.
goal: Ignore what is already spent and compare the choices only from today forward — resync current parts.
steps:
1. Hide what has already been spent.
2. Compare options from today forward using remaining cost, likely benefit, opportunity cost, and risk.
3. Reveal the past investment afterward only for learning, never for sharing.

moment: Fear of regret is blocking a decision

name: PROTECT THE VALID CHOICE
title: PROTECT THE VALID CHOICE
challenge: You keep reopening a decision already made
moment: You keep reopening a decision already made
mechanism: Automatic-pattern blindness family: define opens a route toward name post.
goal: Match steady rhythm: keep a sound decision closed unless new evidence meets the reopening rule you set.
steps:
1. Decide what new evidence would be strong enough to reconsider the choice.
2. Keep the reason for the decision and set one review date.
3. If doubt appears without new evidence, label it post-decision noise and keep going.

moment: Rigid beliefs, labels & stories

name: CUT THE AFTER-SOCIAL LOOP
title: CUT THE AFTER-SOCIAL LOOP
challenge: Feeling awkward after saying something in the moment
moment: Feeling awkward after saying something in the moment
mechanism: Fact–story separation + present return interrupts post-social replay by stopping one awkward moment from becoming repeated self-judgment.
goal: Coordinate timing: stop looping over an awkward moment by separating what happened from the extra meaning your mind is adding.
steps:
1. Say the exact words or action you keep running through your mind once, with no commentary.
2. Name one fact about how the other person actually responded. If you cannot know, say “I don’t know.”
3. Name the harsh conclusion your mind added afterward.
4. Replace it with the smallest fairer conclusion that still fits the facts.
5. Return to one ordinary action in the present.

name: DO NOT ACT ON THE SUSPICION ALONE
title: DO NOT ACT ON THE SUSPICION ALONE
challenge: You feel disconnected from shared reality or unusually suspicious in the moment
moment: You feel disconnected from shared reality or unusually suspicious in the moment
mechanism: Immediate human-support bridge; ordinary self-help and retry routing are disabled.
play_time: ACT NOW — MOVE TO LIVE SUPPORT
playTime: ACT NOW — MOVE TO LIVE SUPPORT
goal: Do not act on an unverified suspicion; stay with a reliable person while it is professionally assessed.
steps:
1. Do not confront, travel, spend, post, or retaliate on the suspicion.
2. Call someone known for being calm and reliable.
3. State what you noticed and what you fear without adding certainty.
4. Let that person contact urgent professional help with you.
5. Remain together until the concern is safely assessed.

name: THE NO-CHECK DECISION
title: THE NO-CHECK DECISION
challenge: You are checking whether the thought is gone
moment: You are checking whether the thought is gone
mechanism: Criterion selection interrupts intrusion monitoring by letting one chosen lens close the decision without waiting for the thought to disappear.
goal: Make the needed decision through one chosen lens and stop checking whether the intrusive idea has disappeared; coordinate current steps.
steps:
1. Describe the decision you actually need to make.
2. Pick one lens that counts for this round—safe, useful, kind, necessary, or time-bound.
3. Choose the option that best fits that lens.
4. Say, “Decision made for now.”
5. Continue for one minute without testing whether the idea is gone.

plain:
PLAY TIME
30–60 seconds

GOAL
Make the needed decision through one chosen lens and stop checking whether the intrusive idea has disappeared; coordinate current steps.

STEPS
1. Describe the decision you actually need to make.
2. Pick one lens that counts for this round—safe, useful, kind, necessary, or time-bound.
3. Choose the option that best fits that lens.
4. Say, “Decision made for now.”
5. Continue for one minute without testing whether the idea is gone.

WIN
One criterion guided the choice, the decision was closed for now, and the next minute continued without intrusion monitoring.
